<reason>B won by holding the debate to actual sanctuary policies rather than an ideal version. A’s trust mechanism was plausible but admittedly uncounted, while B showed the jail loss is structural, that demanding a criminal judicial warrant for civil detainers is a veto, and that bans on even notification force riskier field arrests. A’s reply that strict no-notification cities are mere implementation flaws conceded B’s descriptive point.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s warrant-veto and no-notification rebuttal in R1/R2 was decisive: detainers are civil, notification bans cover robbery/assault/guns, so the loss is not narrow and A’s cooperative ideal does not describe enacted policies.</best_rebuttal>
